projects.name: NODIA
projects.description: Assignment formatting web application. Takes raw university assignment content and formats it into a clean, structurally correct document (headings, citations, references, layout) ready for submission.
projects.problem: University assignments lose marks due to inconsistent formatting: wrong heading hierarchy, missing citations, unreadable layouts, and varying output formats between Word and PDF.
projects.expectedValue: Save 1-2 hours per assignment and produce consistently well-formatted submissions.
projects.v1Scope: Paste assignment text in a browser, format it into clean heading structure with a bibliography, preview the result, and export it as DOCX. Citation detection, PDF export and multiple user accounts are out of scope for V1.
projects.motivation: I spend too long manually formatting assignments instead of spending that time on content. A tool that standardises formatting would save hours per assignment and improve grades.
projects.assumptions: Students are willing to paste their raw content into a web app; most assignments can be normalised into a predictable structure.
projects.initialQuestions: Which output formats matter most? Should it support academic citations?
projects.inspiration: Frustration with an afternoon wasted reformatting an essay in Word.

projects.name: NODEN
projects.description: University-email notification/overlay concept. A lightweight tray/overlay app that watches a university email inbox and surfaces important notices over the desktop without opening the mail client.
projects.problem: Important university emails (deadlines, room changes, cancellations) get buried in the inbox and are missed.
projects.targetUsers: Students relying on university email for time-sensitive notices.
projects.expectedValue: Fewer missed notices; faster reaction to schedule changes.
projects.motivation: Missed a deadline announcement buried under a hundred marketing emails; wanted a watcher that pops notable mail.
projects.assumptions: Users are comfortable authorising inbox access; filters can separate real notices from marketing mail.
projects.initialQuestions: Which mailbox APIs can we use? Can notifications run without a persistent app open?
projects.inspiration: Missed a room-change email 20 minutes before a lecture.

projects.name: NOMAD
projects.description: Idea for a location-aware personal dashboard that surfaces contextually relevant reminders based on where you are (campus, home, transit).
projects.problem: Reminders are time-based only; context such as "when I am on campus" is valuable for student workflows.
projects.targetUsers: Students and commuters with repetitive location patterns.
projects.motivation: Wanted reminders like "grab lab report when you pass the print shop".
projects.initialQuestions: Privacy of location data? Battery impact of geofencing?
projects.inspiration: Missed a print job while already at the lab.

projects.name: WiFi Attendance
projects.description: Attendance tracking by detecting which classroom/club WiFi network a device is connected to at session time.
projects.problem: Manual attendance rolls are error-prone and time-consuming for clubs and small classes.
projects.motivation: A single "connected to this network = present" signal is cheap and unobtrusive.
projects.assumptions: Devices auto-join known networks; one device per person.
projects.initialQuestions: Can people be present without being on the network? How to prevent spoofing?

projects.name: Lost & Found
projects.description: Centralised campus lost-and-found registry: report lost or found items, match by description/location, and coordinate handover.
projects.problem: Lost property is reported to scattered desks with no shared registry, so matching is rare.
projects.expectedValue: More items reunited and a record of the process.
projects.motivation: A friend lost a laptop and the search was entirely manual across six offices.
projects.assumptions: People report items; matching heuristics work with partial descriptions.
projects.initialQuestions: Which attributes make matching reliable? Who moderates?

projects.name: Library Laptop Tracking
projects.description: Sensor/tag-based tracking of laptops loaned from the university library so lost units are found quickly and loans are auditable.
projects.problem: Loaned laptops frequently leave the library building and are hard to locate at return stations.
projects.expectedValue: Locate missing laptops in minutes instead of days.
projects.motivation: The library counts dozens of missing units per term.
projects.assumptions: Tags and readers already deployed in the building.
